questions.q: What are the three Fs that Asprey says drive our prehistoric brain?
a: Fear, feed and reproduction
Fight, flight and freeze
Focus, flow and fun
Food, fitness and family
questions.why: The overview says the brain is wired to keep us alive and passing on our genes, not to make us happy.

questions.q: What question does Asprey suggest asking to decide where to spend your energy?
a: Who do I want to be in twenty years?
What would make me happiest today?
How can I finish this task fastest?
What would my boss expect from me?
questions.why: The first lesson says to prune your to-do list against a picture of your life two decades ahead.

questions.q: What happened to Arianna Huffington after working more than 120 hours a week?
a: She collapsed and broke her cheekbone
She lost control of her company
She was treated for exhaustion twice
She quit and wrote a novel
questions.why: The second lesson uses her collapse to show why sleep and recovery beat burnout.

questions.q: What does Asprey mean by eating like your grandmother?
a: Eat whole, unrefined foods with vegetables and protein
Cook large meals and freeze the leftovers
Follow the recipes handed down in your family
Eat only what you grow yourself
questions.why: The second lesson points to the last generation without industrial food as a model for gut health.

questions.q: What does the summary say about money and happiness?
a: Past a point, more income does not add happiness
Money is the main source of joy for top performers
Wealth guarantees lasting happiness
Happiness falls steadily as income rises
questions.why: The third lesson says the high performers Asprey interviewed treat money as a side effect, not a source of joy.
